text: Git Workbench 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Git 工作台，在侧边栏提供通用仓库面板，并为每个聊天加入 Git、Tickets 和 Board 标签。它通过 Host 路由连接界面与本地 Git 和工作区数据。用户可查看工作区改动、暂存并提交，浏览和切换分支，查看差异与提交历史；还可通过 GitHub 或 GitLab CLI 查看和更新工单、评论及启动拉取请求评审，并在本地看板整理卡片与评论。适合在 DSH 中处理代码仓库、协作工单和个人任务的开发者。看板默认写入本地 DSH 数据目录；工单与评审需要相应的 gh 或 glab 登录。

Git Workbench adds Git, Tickets, and Board tabs to DSH Web. It supports common repository tasks, provider tickets, and a local Kanban board. Developers can manage code and workspace tasks in one interface.
我想在 DSH 里直接暂存文件、提交改动和切换分支。
能不能把 GitHub 或 GitLab 工单放进聊天里查看和评论？
I need a local Kanban board for tasks tied to each DSH workspace.
Git Workbench 的功能「仓库与分支操作」：在 DSH 侧边栏或聊天 Git 标签中查看工作区改动、暂存文件并提交，也可列出和切换分支。用户在对应界面选择操作，插件将请求交给 Host 路由处理。
Git Workbench 的功能「工单与工作区看板」：聊天中的 Tickets 标签连接仓库关联的 GitHub 或 GitLab 工单，可查看、更新和评论；Board 标签则按工作区保存本地卡片与评论，支持独立于 Git 仓库使用。
GitHub 和 GitLab 工单操作经 gh 或 glab CLI 访问对应服务，并使用已登录账户；本地看板内容保存在工作区对应的本机 JSON 文件中。

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · Git Workbench for DeepSeek Harness：A Harness Web plugin for everyday Git work. One bundle provides a general sidebar workbench with repository switching, and every chat gets its own **Git**, **Tickets**, and **Board** view tabs scoped to that chat's workspace.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · Requirements：- An existing DeepSeek Harness installation with plugin support.
- A Git repository for the Git and Tickets views. The Board is local-only and
  works without a repository.
- GitHub CLI (`gh`) for GitHub tickets, reviews and remote operations.
- GitLab CLI (`glab`) for GitLab merge requests and issues.
- Optional: [Plugin Sync](https://github.com/ltfysl/dsh-plugin-sync) to carry
  this plugin to another DSH profile through a secret gist.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · From GitHub：1. Open DSH.
2. Go to **Plugins** in the sidebar.
3. Click **Add plugin** and choose **Install a third-party plugin**.
4. Enter the repository address:

```text
   https://github.com/ltfysl/dsh-git-workbench
   ```

5. Install it and enable **Git Workbench** if DSH asks.
6. Restart DSH if the plugin does not appear immediately.
7. Open **Git** in the sidebar. Each chat now has **Git**, **Tickets**, and
   **Board** tabs.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · From a local checkout：```bash
git clone https://github.com/ltfysl/dsh-git-workbench.git
```

Then use **Plugins → Add plugin → Install a third-party plugin** and enter the
absolute path to the cloned directory. This is also the development workflow.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · First use：- Open a Git repository from the sidebar, or switch to a known workspace.
- For GitHub tickets and reviews, run `gh auth login`. The Host checks every
  authenticated `gh` account and uses one with access to that repository.
- For GitLab tickets, run `glab auth login`.
- Open **Board** for a local Kanban board. It needs no repository and no
  GitHub/GitLab login. Cards live under `~/.dsh/git-workbench/boards`.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · Features：- **Per-chat Git view** — each conversation has a Git tab that opens the repository for that chat's workspace; the sidebar panel remains the general workbench.
- **Working tree** — staged and unstaged changes, stage/unstage individual files or everything, and commit with a message.
- **Quick branch switching** — the branch bar lists recent local branches. It also works from a detached HEAD, asks before carrying uncommitted changes to another branch, and never stashes automatically.
- **Branch browser** — search all local and remote branches without loading hundreds of tabs into the main view. Remote-only branches can be turned into a tracking local branch in one step.
- **Diff window** — click a file to open a VSCode-style dialog with side-by-side or inline hunks, line numbers, additions/deletions, renames, binary files, and truncation notices.
- **History** — recent commits on the branch; click one to inspect its files and diffs.
- **Remote sync** — incoming and outgoing commits, fetch, publish, and a smart sync that fast-forwards and pushes when safe and stops on divergence.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · How it works：The Host half (`index.js`, `lib/git.js`, `lib/tickets.js`, `lib/reviews.js`, `lib/board.js`) registers authenticated Web routes under `/git-workbench`. Git and provider CLIs run through `execFile` with an explicit argument vector, a bounded output buffer, and a timeout — never through a shell. The Client half (`client.js`) registers the sidebar entry, the main panel, and `conversation.view` tabs for each chat, then talks to those routes with same-origin `fetch`. Branch data is split: `/status` carries a capped quick-switch list, while `/branches` loads the complete local/remote branch set only when the branch browser opens. `/switch` and `/branch` validate local refs and create tracking branches without using a shell. Ticket routes (`/tickets`, `/ticket`, `/ticket/labels`, `/ticket/update`, `/ticket/comment`) resolve the provider from the remote and keep access tokens only in child-process environments. Ticket updates cover title, description, state and existing repository labels; no access token enters the browser. @local/dsh-git-workbench README · Tests：```sh
npm test
```

The tests use temporary repositories, a local bare remote, and fake `gh`/`glab` executables. They cover the status branch cap, switching, detached HEAD, remote-only branches, tracking-branch creation, remote/provider detection, GitHub/GitLab listing, comments, create/edit/close, label listing and updates, comment writes, review workspace paths, and local board persistence with comments.

@local/dsh-git-workbench README · Notes：- Sync performs `fetch --all --prune`, then a fast-forward-only merge and/or push.
- Diverged branches are reported instead of merged automatically.
- Branches without an upstream show **Publish branch**.
- Git hooks, credential helpers, and signing configuration are respected.
- GitHub uses the authenticated `gh` CLI; GitLab uses `glab`. If the provider is not authenticated, the Tickets tab explains the exact login command and retries after login.
- New pull requests are intentionally not created from the Tickets view; create them from a branch. PRs/MRs can still be edited, relabeled, closed/reopened, and commented on.
- Review reports are written by the DSH agent into the review worktree. The in-plugin preview disables scripts; the original file remains on disk for opening externally.
- Review prompts default to German and skip the optional awork ticket check. They do not post comments or modify the PR.
- The board is local-only. It does not import tickets, does not require a Git repository, and does not write to GitHub/GitLab.
